events.label: birth
events.text: Lotte Reiniger born in Charlottenburg district of Berlin.

evidence.quote: Lotte Reiniger was born in the Charlottenburg district of Berlin on 2 June 1899

events.label: lecture
events.text: Attended a lecture by Wegener on animation possibilities.

evidence.quote: In 1915 , she attended a lecture by Wegener that focused on the fantastic possibilities of animation

events.text: Animated wooden rats and intertitles for Wegener's Pied Piper film.

evidence.quote: In 1918 , Reiniger animated wooden rats

events.text: Directed her first film, The Ornament of the Enamoured Heart.

evidence.quote: Das Ornament des verliebten Herzens ( The Ornament of the Enamoured Heart , 1919 )

events.text: Began relationship and later marriage with Carl Koch.

evidence.quote: her future creative partner and husband ( from 1921 ) , Carl Koch

events.text: Made fairytale animated short Aschenputtel.

evidence.quote: including the fairytale animation Aschenputtel ( 1922 )

events.text: Louis Hagen approached her to make a feature-length animated film.

evidence.quote: In 1923 , she was approached by Louis Hagen

events.text: The Adventures of Prince Achmed completed.

evidence.quote: The result was The Adventures of Prince Achmed , completed in 1926

events.text: Prince Achmed premiered in Paris after nearly a year without distributor.

evidence.quote: Although it failed to find a distributor for almost a year , once premiered in Paris

events.text: Made Doctor Dolittle und seine Tiere, second feature.

evidence.quote: Doktor Dolittle und seine Tiere ( Doctor Dolittle and his Animals , 1928 )

events.text: Co-directed live-action film Die Jagd nach dem Glück with Rochus Gliese.

evidence.quote: Die Jagd nach dem Glück ( The Pursuit of Happiness , 1929 )

events.text: Die Jagd nach dem Glück release delayed until 1930 for dubbing.

evidence.quote: release of the film was delayed until 1930 to dub in voices by different actors

events.text: Made Carmen, based on Bizet's opera.

evidence.quote: the best-known being Carmen ( 1933 ) and Papageno ( 1935 )

events.text: Began years of exile moving between countries with Koch.

evidence.quote: the couple spent the years 1933–1944 moving from country to country

events.text: Made Papageno, based on Mozart's Die Zauberflöte.

evidence.quote: Papageno ( 1935 )
the best-known being Carmen ( 1933 ) and Papageno ( 1935 )

events.text: Made propaganda film The Golden Goose under Nazi rule.

evidence.quote: One of these films is called ( The Golden Goose , 1944 )

events.text: Left Rome and moved back to Berlin to care for mother.

evidence.quote: they stayed with Visconti in Rome until 1944 , then moved back to Berlin

events.text: Moved with Koch to London.

evidence.quote: In 1949 , Reiniger and Koch moved to London

events.label: founding
events.text: Co-founded Primrose Productions with Louis Hagen Jr.

evidence.quote: they founded Primrose Productions in 1953

events.text: Produced about a dozen Grimm silhouette films for BBC and Telecasting America, 1953-55.

evidence.quote: they founded Primrose Productions in 1953 and , over the next two years , produced more than a dozen short silhouette films

events.text: Provided illustrations for King Arthur and His Knights of the Round Table.

evidence.quote: provided illustrations for the 1953 book King Arthur and His Knights of the Round Table

events.text: Her silhouette children logo used as cover design on TALK magazine.

evidence.quote: One of them was used as cover design on the magazine TALK from 1956

events.text: Husband Carl Koch died; she then entered a period of seclusion.

evidence.quote: After a period of seclusion after her husbands death in 1963

events.text: Published book Shadow Theatres and Shadow Films.

evidence.quote: Shadow Theatres and Shadow Films . London : B.T . Batsford Ltd. , 1970

events.label: award
events.text: Awarded the Deutscher Filmpreis.

evidence.quote: Reiniger was awarded the of the Deutscher Filmpreis in 1972

events.label: honour
events.text: Received the Great Cross of the Order of Merit of Germany.

evidence.quote: in 1979 she received the Great Cross of the Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany

events.text: Completed Die vier Jahreszeiten, her last film.

evidence.quote: the last of which , Die vier Jahreszeiten , was completed the year before she died
Reiniger died in Dettenhausen , Germany , on 19 June 1981

events.label: death
events.text: Lotte Reiniger died in Dettenhausen, Germany.

evidence.quote: Reiniger died in Dettenhausen , Germany , on 19 June 1981

undated_mentions: As a child, built her own puppet theatre for family shows
Enrolled in the acting group of Max Reinhardt's Theatre, undated
Admitted to the Institut für Kulturforschung after the Pied Piper success
Made silhouette falcon special effects for Fritz Lang's Die Nibelungen
Abandoned a third animated feature based on Ravel's opera
Worked on several films with Eric Walter White
Decided with Koch to emigrate after the rise of the Nazi Party
Forced to make propaganda films under Nazi rule
Made short advertising films for the GPO Film Unit in London
Early 1950s: became friends with Freddy Bloom in London
Early 1950s: designed a logo for TALK at Bloom's request
Early 1950s: worked at Beconsfield studios, Buckinghamshire
Returned to Germany after seclusion following husband's death
Visited the United States and began making films again after 1963
